Control-flow analysis can follow aliased conditions/discriminants; destructured discriminated unions and dependent rest-tuple parameters can retain correlations.
Narrowing can be preserved in non-hoisted closures after the last assignment when no nested function invalidates that analysis.
Eligible functions can infer type predicate return types; effectively constant obj[key] expressions can be narrowed after checks.

sourceSnapshot.authority: Official TypeScript Handbook and release notes

accuracyFacts: TypeScript 5.5 only infers a type predicate when the function has no explicit return type or predicate, one return statement and no implicit return, does not mutate its parameter, and returns a boolean expression tied to a refinement. Inferred predicates carry if-and-only-if semantics; truthiness of number|string|nullish values may fail the false-direction condition.
A user-written type predicate is trusted and is not verified by the compiler; an incorrect predicate can make later code unsound. Assertion signatures are likewise promises by their implementations.
TypeScript 5.5 narrows obj[key] after a check when both obj and key are effectively constant; later assignments invalidate the relevant stability premise.
TypeScript 5.4 can preserve narrowing in non-hoisted closures after a last assignment, but analysis does not apply if the variable is assigned in a nested function.

The in operator can retain a type with an optional property in both true and false branches because optional properties may be present or absent. A true check does not mean the property value is non-undefined.
typeof null is object in JavaScript, so typeof checks alone do not remove null from an object union.
Control-flow narrowing is static reasoning based on code paths, not runtime validation or a guarantee that untyped external data matches its declaration.
